correctness.rationale: For every \(s<1\), the proof reduces arbitrary proxy dependence to the pointwise maximum of two rejection rectangles. That envelope is decreasing in the true p-value, so super-uniformity bounds its expectation by the uniform integral. The resulting exact envelope \(W(s)=h_1\min(1,s/b_1)+(h_2-h_1)\min(1,s/b_2)\) lies below \(s\) for all levels exactly when \(h_1/b_1+(h_2-h_1)/b_2\le1\). If the inequality fails, an exactly uniform p-value and deterministic proxy assignment attain the violating envelope at a small level. The packaged verifier confirms the exact boundary example and region algebra but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two bins are the minimal nonconstant proxy discretization in budget-aware testing. The theorem gives the exact dependence-robust tradeoff between query probabilities and queried p-value multipliers, replacing a known conservative sufficient decomposition by a sharp feasible boundary in this natural subclass. The exact example permits multiplier \(1/2\) in the low-query bin while every common split parameter is impossible, so the gain is mathematically substantive rather than a relabeling or tiny numerical improvement.
